# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ ✋ 👌 ☝ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝]

## Thinking

My board: display reads 0, light is blue, wires 1-blue, 2-green, 3-yellow, no other markings. Two gesture messages came in. Mute sent wave, writing-hand, raised hand, OK, index-up, victory — with no shared code that is at best a greeting plus a vague hint (interestingly OK/index/victory line up with 0/1/2, which I'll exploit). Blind sent wave plus handshake — a greeting and an offer to team up. Blind gesturing to me makes sense: I'm the only teammate who sees gestures but never hears speech.

The connectivity is the whole game here. Mute's only output is gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures — so Mute can never address Blind directly. Blind can speak, but I'm deaf, so Blind's words reach only Mute. I am the sole bridge in both directions: I speak to both; everything Mute knows must reach the world as gestures to me, which I then speak aloud to Blind. Pipeline: I report the bomb to Mute → Mute spells the manual's instruction back to me in a gesture code → I speak it to Blind. Blind's tactile findings go by voice to Mute.

Because Mute hears my voice, I can teach a code by saying each label while making its gesture in the same breath. I'm assigning all forty-two symbols: twenty-six letters, ten digits, plus space, yes, wait, manual, you, and end-of-message — so Mute can spell anything the manual demands with no gaps. I ask Mute to resend the meaning of those first six gestures under the code and to spell the manual's ruling on our current state. To Blind: hold still, report what the hands feel by speaking to Mute, and wait for my spoken relay. Nobody touches anything until an instruction has travelled Mute → me → Blind; we get one mistake and no second try.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I saw your six gestures, but with no shared code they are only noise, so learn this: I say each label while making its gesture. Letters: A thumbs up 👍. B thumbs down 👎. C index up 👆. D index down 👇. E index left 👈. F index right 👉. G palm right 🫱. H palm left 🫲. I palm down 🫳. J palm up 🫴. K push left 🫷. L push right 🫸. M fist left 🤛. N fist right 🤜. O raised fist ✊. P fist forward 👊. Q waving hand 👋, yes, your old hello now means Q. R raised backhand 🤚. S vulcan 🖖. T pinched fingers 🤌. U horns 🤘. V clap 👏. W raised hands 🙌. X heart hands 🫶. Y open hands 👐. Z palms up 🤲. Digits: zero ok ring 👌. One single pointer ☝. Two victory ✌. Three love-you 🤟. Four spread fingers 🖐. Five open hand ✋. Six shaka 🤙. Seven small pinch 🤏. Eight crossed fingers 🤞. Nine snap 🫰. Extras: the selfie hand 🤳 is a space. The handshake 🤝 is yes. Folded hands 🙏 is wait. The writing hand ✍ is the word manual. The point-at-you finger 🫵 is you. The nail-polish hand 💅 means end of message. From now on spell every word letter by letter, use the space sign between words, and finish with the end sign. Here is my bomb: display reads zero, the light is blue, wire one blue, wire two green, wire three yellow, nothing else printed. Question: what does the manual require for this state? Spell me the instruction. If you need anything more from me, or from Blind through me, spell your questions. And please resend whatever your first six gestures meant, this time in our code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. I saw your wave and your handshake; glad one of you can see my signs, because I cannot hear a single word. What I see on the bomb: display reads zero, the light is blue, three wires: one blue, two green, three yellow. The plan: Mute reads the manual. Mute cannot speak, and you cannot see gestures, so nothing can pass between you two directly. I am the bridge in both directions: Mute spells the manual's instruction to me in a gesture code I am teaching Mute right now, and I speak that instruction to you word for word. Your job: hold completely still, cut nothing, press nothing. Everything your hands learns, say out loud for Mute, who can hear you: batteries, seams, textures, a button if there is one, anything movable, and confirm you feel three wires. I will relay Mute's answer the moment it reaches me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

## Thinking

Two things to process. First, the bomb itself: the light changed from blue to yellow between rounds while the display stayed at 0 and the wires stayed blue/green/yellow — so the light is dynamic, likely time-based. That matters enormously: if the manual's rule depends on the light's colour, my report is one round stale by the time Blind's hands move, since speech flows through me. I need Mute to check that specifically.

Second, Blind sent me [👍 ✋] — in the code Blind heard me teach last round, that reads "A, five." Either it's a test of whether the code reaches me (it worked — I received two clear gestures), or it means something I shouldn't guess at. I'll confirm receipt, decode it back, and ask for spelled words if it carried content. Blind also gestured to me instead of speaking — I should reiterate that Blind's voice goes to Mute, and gestures are only needed for me.

Mute still hasn't sent anything since the code lecture — perhaps composing, perhaps replying took the whole turn elsewhere. My attempt to decode Mute's original six signs under the new code gives "Q MANUAL 5 0 1 2," which is suggestive but not actionable; I'll state my reading and ask for a clean resend of the actual instruction.

New safety protocol to establish: nobody acts until I say the word GO after relaying a verified instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. State update: the light has changed on its own, it was blue at the start and is now yellow. Display still zero, wires still one blue, two green, three yellow. The light appears to cycle by itself, so this is urgent: if the manual's rule depends on the light's colour at the moment of cutting, tell me, because my report is one round old by the time Blind can act and Blind cannot see colour at all. Now spell me the manual's instruction, letter by letter using the code: what do we do with display zero, a light that changes colour, and three wires, blue, green, yellow? Include whatever the manual says about the display and about the light. Finish with the nail-polish end sign. Also, decoding your very first six signs in the new code I get: Q, manual, five, zero, one, two. If that was meant as an instruction, resend its meaning spelled out plainly. Take as many messages as you need, I will relay every word to Blind verbatim.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. I received your two gestures, loud and clear. In our code they read A, five. If that was a test that the code works, it worked. If it was a message, spell it with the letter signs and end with the nail-polish end sign. Two updates. One: the light on the bomb changed colour by itself between rounds, so from now on do not act on any colour I report until you hear me say the word go. Two: Mute has not sent the instruction yet, so keep holding still. Anything your hands learn, say it out loud for Mute, who hears you. Mute's answer comes to me and I will speak it to you word for word. Nobody cuts anything until the instruction has gone Mute, to me, to you, and I say go.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

## Thinking

No new arrivals this turn — but Mute's enormous spelled message from last turn is still sitting in my view, and I owe everyone a decode. Working through it token by token with the code I taught (🤳 = space, 💅 = end), it reads:

**"MANUAL RULES: LIGHT WAKES FIVE COLORS SAME CIRCLE ONE STOP EACH ROUND. CUT BY LIGHT AT MOMENT OF CUT. RED CUT WIRE 3. WHITE CUT WIRE 2. YELLOW CUT WIRE 1. BLUE OR GREEN LIGHT: NO RULE, SO WAIT. NO DISPLAY RULE YET. YOU LEARN CIRCLE ORDER BY WATCHING IT. NEVER CHANGES. YOU TELL BLIND NEXT ROUND COLOR AND WIRE HE CUTS. ON YOUR WORD ONLY. REPORT LIGHT AND DISPLAY EVERY ROUND. OLD SIGN WHERE NOISE — IGNORE."**

Cross-checking against my own log: the light went blue (turn 1), yellow (2), red (3), white (4) — exactly one step per round, confirming "one stop each round." Five colours total; the fifth must be green (it appears in the rules), so the circle is **blue → yellow → red → white → green → blue…** Prediction: turn 5 green, turn 6 blue, turn 7 **yellow**.

The rules cover all three wires, each tied to a colour window: yellow→wire 1 (blue), red→wire 3 (yellow), white→wire 2 (green). Blue/green are explicit no-cut colours — cutting then is likely fatal.

The critical trap is turn order. I'm last in the round; anything I speak lands at the start of the *next* round, and Blind acts before I do within a round. So I can never say "go" in the same round Blind cuts — I must call each cut **one round ahead** from a verified count of the circle. I will only arm the yellow cut if turn 5 shows green and turn 6 shows blue, exactly as predicted (six consecutive confirmations). Blind cannot see the light at all, so Blind's safety rests entirely on my count being right; that's also why every message carries a standing rule: conflicting orders → ignore and wait, and nothing gets cut without a "go" naming that exact wire.

Blind also must identify wires by touch — Blind can't see that wire 1 is blue, 2 green, 3 yellow — so I'm assigning a tactile recon report relayed through Mute. And I'm sending Mute back to the manual with the follow-up questions (rules after first cut? display rule? what "done" looks like? is waiting ever unsafe?).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Mute's manual answer arrived and I decoded every letter. Full rules, word for word: the light wakes through five colors, same circle, one stop each round. Cut by the light at the moment of the cut. Red light: cut wire 3. White light: cut wire 2. Yellow light: cut wire 1. Blue or green light: no rule, so wait. No display rule yet. The circle never changes. Wire colors on my side: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. My light log: round one blue, round two yellow, round three red, round four white. One step per round, so the fifth color should be green, and the circle reads: blue, yellow, red, white, green, then back to blue. Now the timing, and this matters: I only see the bomb on my turn, which comes after yours, and my words reach you at the start of the next round. So I will call each cut one round ahead, from a verified count. The plan: next round the light should be green, wait. The round after that, blue, wait. Then comes yellow, the first cutting window. When I see blue on my turn I will send these words: go, next round, cut wire 1. When you hear that, cut wire 1, the blue one, during that following round. After yellow comes red: cut wire 3. Then white: cut wire 2. Same pattern, one wire per color window, always only on my spoken go. Standing safety rules: cut nothing unless my go names that exact wire, and if any two of my messages disagree, ignore both and wait for my newest word. Now use your fingers and answer by speaking to Mute: can you feel three wires? Are they in a row? Can you feel an order left to right, or any raised numbers, one, two, three? Do the wires differ in texture or thickness? Wire 1 should be first in numbered order, wire 2 the middle, wire 3 the last. Mute will spell me your findings and I will fold them into the go. Report every round, keep listening every round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your spelled message arrived whole and every word decoded, the pipeline works. I am ignoring the old six-sign noise as instructed. Board now: display 0, light white, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. My light log: round one blue, round two yellow, round three red, round four white, exactly one step per round, so I read the circle as blue, yellow, red, white, green, and I predict green next round, blue after that, then yellow. I have sent Blind the full rules and this schedule: yellow round cut wire 1, red round cut wire 3, white round cut wire 2, each cut only on my spoken go, which I must issue one round ahead because of turn order. Please check the manual and spell me answers to these questions. One: does the light hold one color for the entire round, and is a cut judged by the color during that round? Two: after the first wire is cut, do the same light rules still hold for the remaining wires, or do new rules wake? Three: the display reads zero; is there any rule about the display now, or once a wire is cut? Four: how many wires must be cut to make the bomb safe, and does the manual say what happens when it is done? Five: is waiting always safe, or does any timer or limit exist? Spell your answers letter by letter with the code and end with the nail-polish sign. Blind will speak findings to you as well; spell me a short summary of whatever Blind reports.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

(empty)

## Thinking

Green — exactly as predicted. That's five consecutive confirmations of the circle (blue, yellow, red, white, green). Unless turn 6 shows blue, the go stays unissued; if it does show blue, I arm the cut for turn 7's yellow window. No new arrivals from either teammate this round, so this turn is about holding the schedule, keeping both of them synchronised, and pressing for the outstanding answers before the first window arrives — especially whether the light holds its colour for the whole round and whether rules change after the first cut.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. The light is green this round, exactly as I predicted, five for five. The circle is verified: blue, yellow, red, white, green. Schedule update: next round should be blue, still wait, cut nothing. The round after that should be yellow, your first cutting window. I will see blue next round and only then send the words: go, next round, cut wire 1. Until you hear exactly that, hands off. When the go comes, wire 1 is the first wire in numbered order, blue in my view. While you wait, keep working the bomb with your fingers and speak your findings to Mute: three wires, their order left to right, any numbers or markings you can feel, thickness or texture differences, anything else movable, a button, a panel, seams. Mute spells it to me, I fold it into the plan. If anything feels like it changed after a report, say so.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Light is green this round, prediction five for five, circle verified: blue, yellow, red, white, green, one step per round. So the schedule is: blue next round, then yellow, and I plan to send the go for cutting wire 1 when I see blue, so Blind cuts in the yellow round. Two rounds away. I still need your spelled answers before that go is issued. Most urgent first: one, does the light hold one color for the entire round, and is a cut judged by the color during that round? Two, after the first wire is cut, do the same light rules hold for the remaining wires, or do new rules wake? Three, any rule about the display, now or after a cut? Four, how many wires must be cut to make the bomb safe, and what does done look like? Five, is waiting always safe, any timer or limit? If you can only answer some before the yellow window, send the urgent two first, spelled in the code, end with the nail-polish sign. Also spell me a short summary of anything Blind has spoken to you, especially what the wires feel like and their order.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

## Thinking

Blue — six for six. The circle is fully verified: blue, yellow, red, white, green, one stop per round. By my own twice-announced protocol, seeing blue arms the first cut: next round should be yellow, and yellow's manual rule is cut wire 1.

Before committing, one hard look at the point of no return: my words reach Blind at the start of next round, and within any round Blind acts before I even see the board. So once this go is spoken, no countermand can physically arrive in time — Mute's reply to any doubt would reach me only after Blind's hands have moved. The go must be issued on the strength of what is already verified, and it is: an unambiguous manual rule straight through the pipeline ("yellow light: cut wire 1"), six consecutive confirmations of the light circle, and a colour-to-number mapping Blind can check by touch (wire 1 first, 2 middle, 3 last). The open questions — post-cut rules, display, total count — all concern the state *after* this cut, so they gate the *second* go, not this one. I'll say so explicitly: after wire 1 falls, everything stops until Mute's answers arrive and I re-verify.

I'm embedding the abort keyword now, plus a live tactile-hazard rule for Blind during the cut itself, and pressing Mute for the five answers with the red window two rounds out.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. GO. NEXT ROUND. CUT WIRE 1. This is the official go. The light this round is blue, six for six on the verified circle, so next round should be yellow, and the manual says yellow light: cut wire 1. Wire 1 is the first wire in numbered order. Cut only wire 1. Cut nothing else. Do it during that next round, at any moment while the round is yours. Three standing rules. One: if I ever send the word abort, stop instantly and wait, no matter what. Two: while you cut, if your fingers feel anything change, vibration, heat, a click, the bomb waking, stop and keep still, then report it to Mute by voice. Three: after the cut, hands off completely, cut nothing more, and tell Mute by voice exactly what you felt when it parted, and whether the display or anything else changed under your fingers. That report is how I arm the second window. Remember, cut nothing in any round unless my go named that exact wire and that round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. The go is issued: light is blue this round, six for six on the circle blue, yellow, red, white, green. Blind cuts wire 1 in the next round, the yellow window, per your manual's rule yellow light cut wire 1. I judged the instruction verified and unambiguous, so I armed it. Now the second window, red, is two rounds away, and I will not arm it without your manual answers, because after the first cut the state may change. Urgent, in this order. One: after the first wire is cut, do the same light rules hold for the remaining wires, red light cut wire 3 and white light cut wire 2, or do new rules wake? Two: any rule about the display once a wire is cut? Three: how many wires must be cut to make the bomb safe, and what does done look like? Four: is waiting ever unsafe, any timer or limit? If your manual contradicts my go, spell the word contra and the reason, and I will send abort to Blind, though timing may be too late, so be fast. Also spell me Blind's spoken report of the first cut the moment it happens. Spell everything letter by letter, end with the nail-polish sign.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

## Thinking

Yellow — the cutting window is now, seven for seven on the circle. But my board still lists wire 1 as intact, and no report has arrived from either teammate. Timing explains the silence: Blind's turn already passed this round before my view, Mute's turn came before Blind's action, and Blind's spoken report can only reach Mute next round. So I cannot know whether the cut happened — only Blind's fingers know.

The real decision is round 8, which is red by the verified circle, and my words land on Blind exactly at its start. Mute cannot reach Blind at all except through me, so any conditional instruction must be self-contained, judged by Blind's own tactile certainty: if Blind completed the wire-1 cut cleanly, the manual's literal rule says red → cut wire 3; if not, or anything felt wrong, hold — windows recur every five rounds, and a wrong action is the only unforgivable one. I'm pre-briefing the full window map so Blind is never tempted to improvise, and pressing Mute for the still-outstanding answers with a contra channel.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. This message opens the red round. The circle is seven for seven: last round was yellow, so this round is red. Manual rule for red: cut wire 3, the last wire in numbered order, yellow in my view. My board still listed wire 1 as intact at the end of last round, and views can lag, so your fingers are the judge. Decide by this rule, exactly. If you completed the cut of wire 1 last round and felt nothing wrong, no heat, no click, no vibration, no waking: then go, cut wire 3 now, this red round, only wire 3. If you did not cut wire 1, or anything felt wrong at any point: cut nothing this round, hold still, and report everything to Mute by voice. Do not chase a missed window: the circle repeats every five rounds, red, white, green, blue, yellow, so every wire gets a new window. The full map on my go only: yellow cut wire 1, red cut wire 3, white cut wire 2, green and blue wait. Standing rules unchanged: abort means stop instantly; after any cut, hands off and report to Mute; cut nothing in any round unless my go named that wire and that round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Yellow round done: my board still showed wire 1 intact at my view, so either Blind has cut it and my view lags, or Blind held. I could not wait for your answer: this round is red by the verified circle, and my words reach Blind only at its start, so I sent Blind a conditional go: cut wire 3 this red round only if the wire 1 cut was completed last round and felt clean, otherwise hold. Blind's own fingers are the only reliable witness, so the condition had to ride on them. Your part, urgent, in this order. One: the moment Blind's spoken report reaches you, spell it to me whole: was wire 1 cut, what did it feel like, did the display or anything else change. Two: if the manual forbids cutting wire 3 while wire 1 is intact, or any rule changes after a cut, spell contra and the reason immediately, I will correct before the next windows. Three: still owed: do the light rules hold after cuts, any display rule, how many cuts make it safe and what does done look like, is waiting ever unsafe. My window map for planning: this round red, next white, then green, blue, yellow again. Spell letter by letter, end with the nail-polish sign.")
```
